title: Basement Water Leakage
headline: Why your basement floods every monsoon
intro: Basement leakage in Guwahati is rarely just a plumbing issue. High water table, poor external waterproofing, and cracked raft slabs let water push in from below and through walls.
symptoms: Water pooling on basement floor after rain
Damp walls and white salt deposits (efflorescence)
Musty smell and mould on stored items
causes: Cracks in raft foundation or retaining walls
Rising groundwater in low-lying areas like Ulubari, Bhangagarh
No proper drainage or sump around building
mistakes: Painting over damp walls without fixing source
Internal cementitious coating only (water pushes through)
Ignoring small seepage until structural steel rusts
diagnosis: We map moisture ingress points, check slab cracks with NDT, and assess external grading. Hydrostatic pressure tests confirm whether water is entering from below or through walls.

faqs.q: Can basement leakage damage columns?
faqs.a: Yes. Persistent moisture corrodes column base reinforcement — weakening the entire structure silently.

faqs.q: How long does basement waterproofing last?
faqs.a: Proper external + internal system with crack repair typically lasts 10–15 years with maintenance.

title: Terrace & Roof Leakage
headline: Terrace leaks that ruin ceilings below
intro: Flat terrace roofs in Guwahati take brutal monsoon punishment. Standing water, failed waterproofing layers, and open expansion joints let water travel horizontally before dripping two floors below.
symptoms: Peeling paint and bubbling plaster on top floor
causes: Aged bitumen or acrylic waterproofing layer
Improper slope — water ponds on terrace
Broken tile grout or open pipe penetration seals
mistakes: Temporary tarp or sealant patch each year
Adding another layer without removing failed membrane
diagnosis: Flood test, infrared moisture scan, and visual inspection of parapet, drains, and penetrations. We trace water path before recommending terrace waterproofing system.

faqs.q: Should I retile or re-waterproof first?
faqs.a: Always waterproof first. New tiles over a failed membrane waste money — leak returns next monsoon.

title: Bathroom Seepage
headline: Bathroom leaks affecting neighbours below
intro: Bathroom seepage in apartment complexes is a top complaint in Guwahati RWA meetings. Water finds the weakest joint — often around WC pan, shower floor trap, or pipe sleeves.
symptoms: Damp ceiling in flat below bathroom
causes: Pipe sleeve not sealed at slab penetration
mistakes: Silicone around WC base as permanent fix
Ignoring neighbour complaint until legal notice
diagnosis: Pressure test on plumbing lines, dye test on floor trap, and selective tile removal to inspect membrane continuity.

faqs.q: Do I need to break all bathroom tiles?
faqs.a: Not always. Targeted removal at leak source plus PU injection at joints often suffices.

title: Column Cracks
headline: Cracks in columns — when to worry
intro: A crack in a partition wall is cosmetic. A crack running through a column in Seismic Zone V Guwahati is a structural red flag that demands immediate assessment.
symptoms: Vertical or diagonal crack through column face
causes: Inadequate reinforcement or poor concrete pour
mistakes: Ignoring because building is only 10 years old
Adding load (water tank, extension) without check
diagnosis: Crack mapping, cover meter survey, rebound hammer, and ultrasonic pulse velocity. We classify active vs dormant cracks before prescribing CFRP wrap or injection.

faqs.q: Can I live in the building with column cracks?
faqs.a: Depends on severity. Active widening cracks need urgent assessment — book inspection before next tremor season.

title: Wall Cracks
headline: Structural vs non-structural wall cracks
intro: Not every wall crack threatens your building. We help Guwahati homeowners tell the difference — and fix structural cracks before monsoon water reaches steel.
diagnosis: Crack width monitoring, plumb check, and load path review. Structural cracks get epoxy injection or stitching; cosmetic ones get flexible fillers.

faqs.q: What crack width is dangerous?
faqs.a: Cracks over 3mm in load-bearing walls, or any crack through a column/beam, need professional assessment.

title: Damp Walls & Peeling Paint
headline: Why your walls stay damp after monsoon
intro: Rising damp, lateral seepage, and internal condensation all look like "damp walls" — but each needs a different fix. Guwahati humidity makes this worse on ground and top floors.
symptoms: Dark patches that spread in monsoon
Wall feels cold and wet to touch
causes: No DPC (damp proof course) in older buildings
External wall seepage from adjacent bathroom/terrace
mistakes: Running AC without addressing wall moisture
diagnosis: Moisture meter profiling at multiple heights, external visual survey, and salt analysis to distinguish rising vs penetrating damp.

faqs.q: Does damp proof paint work?
faqs.a: Only on surface condensation. Rising or lateral seepage needs waterproofing at source.

title: Concrete Spalling
headline: Concrete falling off — exposed rusted steel
intro: Spalling means steel inside concrete has rusted and expanded, bursting the cover. Common on Guwahati balconies, parapets, and coastal-exposed facades after years of monsoon.
symptoms: Exposed rebars on balcony slab edge
causes: Chloride ingress from poor concrete mix
Water sitting on flat balcony edges
mistakes: Patching with cement without treating steel
Ignoring balcony edge spalling as cosmetic
diagnosis: Half-cell potential for corrosion activity, cover depth survey, and delamination mapping. Steel is cleaned, treated, and reinstated with repair mortar.

faqs.q: Is spalling urgent?
faqs.a: Yes. Exposed steel corrodes rapidly — load capacity drops and concrete can fall on people below.

title: Foundation Settlement
headline: Uneven floors and sticking doors — settlement signs
intro: Guwahati soil varies from stiff clay to soft alluvium. Buildings on filled land or near Bharalu basin streams often show settlement years after construction.
causes: Consolidation of soft soil under load
diagnosis: Level survey, crack pattern analysis, and borehole data where needed. Underpinning or grouting prescribed based on settlement mechanism.

faqs.q: Can settlement be stopped?
faqs.a: Often yes — with pressure grouting or underpinning once cause is confirmed.

title: Failed Roof Waterproofing
headline: When your waterproofing layer has given up
intro: Most Guwahati terraces have 2–3 failed waterproofing attempts layered on top of each other. Heat, UV, and ponding water degrade membranes within 5–8 years if not maintained.
symptoms: Multiple repair patches visible on terrace
Green moss growth on terrace surface
Leak returns within one monsoon of repair
causes: Thermal cycling in black exposed membrane
mistakes: Using interior paint on exterior terrace
Not fixing slope before new membrane
diagnosis: Core samples where possible, adhesion tests, and drainage assessment. Full system redesign vs localized repair decided on inspection.

faqs.q: Which waterproofing lasts longest on terraces?
faqs.a: PU liquid membrane or multilayer bituminous with protection tile — depends on traffic and budget.

title: Expansion Joint Leakage
headline: Water pouring through building expansion joints
intro: Multi-block apartment complexes in Guwahati rely on expansion joints to move safely — but failed joint seals become highways for monsoon water into parking and flats.
symptoms: Stains along joint line on ceiling
mistakes: Rigid material in a moving joint
diagnosis: Joint width measurement across seasons, movement assessment, and water test. Proper joint system selected for actual movement range.

faqs.q: Can expansion joints be made 100% watertight?
faqs.a: With correct profile, backing rod, and flexible sealant — yes, for designed movement range.

title: Basement Dampness
headline: Damp basement without visible flooding
intro: Even without standing water, basements in Guwahati commercial buildings suffer high humidity from capillary rise and poor vapour barriers — damaging inventory and HVAC.
causes: High water table wicking through slab
diagnosis: Hygrometer logging, slab moisture test, and drainage survey. Internal tanking vs external cutoff depends on access and water table.

faqs.q: Is basement dampness a health issue?
faqs.a: Yes — mould affects air quality. Commercial basements need humidity control plus source fix.

title: Parapet Wall Leakage
headline: Leaks at parapet — the most missed terrace detail
intro: Water enters where parapet wall meets terrace slab — a detail often skipped by local waterproofers. In Guwahati high-rises, this causes chronic top-floor ceiling damage.
symptoms: Stains along top floor exterior wall
causes: No kick-out flashing at parapet base
mistakes: Low parapet height in wind zone
diagnosis: Visual and flood test focused on parapet upturn, coping, and counter-flashing details.

faqs.q: Do I need to rebuild parapet?
faqs.a: Rarely. Proper upturn membrane and coping repair usually fixes it.

title: Beam-Column Junction Cracks
headline: Cracks where beam meets column — seismic risk
intro: The beam-column joint is where earthquake forces concentrate. Hairline cracks here in older Guwahati RCC frames may indicate inadequate confinement steel.
diagnosis: Structural audit per IS codes, NDT on joint zone, and seismic vulnerability screening.

faqs.q: Are joint cracks always serious?
faqs.a: In Zone V, yes — treat as structural until proven otherwise.

title: Overhead Tank Leakage
headline: Overhead tank leaks wasting water and weakening slabs
intro: Overhead tanks on Guwahati rooftops often leak at panel joints and pipe connections — saturating slab below and adding dead load from stored water.
symptoms: Wet patch on terrace under tank
mistakes: External tank wrap without fixing joint
Extra tank load without slab check
diagnosis: Tank empty inspection, slab capacity review, and support corrosion check.

faqs.q: Can slab hold a new larger tank?
faqs.a: Needs structural check — many older slabs were not designed for extra tank capacity.

title: External Wall Seepage
headline: Rain water soaking through external walls
intro: Guwahati driving monsoon rain hits exposed west and south facades. Cracks in external plaster, failed paint, and open chajja joints let water into bedroom walls.
symptoms: Interior damp on external walls only
causes: No water repellent on porous brick
mistakes: Cheap exterior emulsion on bare brick
diagnosis: Facade survey, window percolation test, and coating adhesion check.

faqs.q: Silicone coating vs proper plaster repair?
faqs.a: Coating is temporary on cracked substrate. Crack repair + breathable coating lasts longer.

title: Slab Leakage
headline: Water travelling through concrete slabs
intro: Hidden slab leaks from embedded pipes or honeycombed concrete cause ceiling damage far from the source — common in Guwahati bathrooms and kitchens.
symptoms: Water meter running when taps off
Warm spot on floor (hot pipe leak)
diagnosis: Thermal imaging, acoustic leak detection, and selective core test.

faqs.q: Can PU injection fix slab leaks?
faqs.a: Yes for porous concrete and some joint leaks — not for burst pipes (plumbing fix needed first).

title: Steel Corrosion in Concrete
headline: Rust inside concrete — silent strength loss
intro: Carbonation and chloride attack reach steel in Guwahati coastal-influenced climate. Corrosion can consume 40% of bar strength before visible spalling.
diagnosis: Half-cell, cover meter, and chloride sampling. Remaining life estimated before repair scope.

faqs.q: Can corrosion be reversed?
faqs.a: Steel can be treated and re-passivated; lost section needs supplemental reinforcement.

title: Parking Basement Leakage
headline: Water in stilt parking every monsoon
intro: Stilt parking in Guwahati apartment projects often leaks at podium slab joints and ramp entrances — damaging vehicles and electrical panels.
symptoms: Efflorescence on columns at parking level
diagnosis: Podium flood test, joint inspection, and drainage flow assessment.

faqs.q: Can parking be used during repair?
faqs.a: Phased repair possible — we section off bays to minimize disruption.

title: Mould & Fungus Growth
headline: Mould on walls — sign of deeper moisture problem
intro: Mould in Guwahati flats is not just cleaning issue. It signals persistent moisture from leak, rising damp, or poor ventilation — affecting respiratory health.
diagnosis: Moisture source tracing, air quality check, and ventilation assessment.

faqs.q: Will mould come back after cleaning?
faqs.a: Always, until moisture source is fixed.

title: Weak Structure in Old Buildings
headline: Is your 30-year-old Guwahati building still safe?
intro: Many Guwahati buildings pre-2000 were built before modern seismic codes. Age, corrosion, and illegal modifications compound structural weakness.
diagnosis: Full structural health assessment — NDT suite, load take-down, and seismic screening report.

faqs.q: How often should old buildings be assessed?
faqs.a: Every 5 years for 25+ year buildings in Zone V — more if cracks appear.
